The Splunk Add-on for Google Cloud Platform's Source types page (splunk.github.io, Splunk product documentation) is cited separately for the sourcetype's own description and its CIM status; no text from it is quoted.

cite.title: Source types - Splunk Add-on for Google Cloud Platform

finding.proto.title: Security Command Center v1 API: Finding message (finding.proto)

notification_message.proto.title: Security Command Center v1 API: NotificationMessage message (notification_message.proto)

resource.proto.title: Security Command Center v1 API: Resource message (resource.proto)

envelope_publish_time.format: Epoch seconds with a fractional (millisecond) part; the modular input's own pull time.

finding_name.format: A relative resource name: organizations/{id}/sources/{id}/findings/{id} (or folders/... or projects/...).

finding_parent.format: A relative resource name one level up from the finding: organizations/{id}/sources/{id}.
finding_parent.quote: The relative resource name of the source the finding belongs to.

finding_resource_name.format: A full resource name (//service.googleapis.com/path) for the Google Cloud resource the finding is about.
finding_resource_name.quote: For findings on Google Cloud resources, the full resource name of the Google Cloud resource this finding is for.

ACTIVE.meaning: The security issue the finding describes has not been addressed.
ACTIVE.quote: The finding requires attention and has not been addressed yet.

INACTIVE.meaning: The finding was fixed, triaged as a non-issue, or otherwise addressed.
INACTIVE.quote: The finding has been fixed, triaged as a non-issue or otherwise addressed and is no longer active.

finding_category.format: A detector-assigned string; casing and spacing vary by detector (Security Health Analytics uses UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, Event Threat Detection uses a human-readable phrase).
finding_category.quote: The additional taxonomy group within findings from a given source.

PUBLIC_BUCKET_ACL.meaning: A Cloud Storage bucket's ACL grants access to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers, so anyone on the internet (or any authenticated Google account) can read it.
PUBLIC_BUCKET_ACL.note: Paraphrased from the finding's own sourceProperties.Explanation in the pubsub2inbox fixture, not a vendor category table (Security Command Center does not publish one).

Malware: Bad Domain.meaning: A resource looked up or connected to a domain on a known-bad list, per the sourceProperties.properties.domains value in the fixture.
Malware: Bad Domain.note: From security-response-automation-rego-fixtures-v1.json, a sample present in the pack's sample directory but not listed among entry.json's provenanced datasets; treat the exact vendor wording as unconfirmed.

finding_external_uri.format: Empty, or a well-formed URL to a Cloud Console page.

finding_event_time.quote: The time the finding was first detected.

finding_create_time.quote: The time at which the finding was created in Security Command Center.

finding_security_marks_name.format: The finding's own name with /securityMarks appended.

examples.value: This bucket is public and can be accessed by anyone on the Internet. "allUsers" represents anyone on the Internet, and "allAuthenticatedUsers" represents anyone who is authenticated with a Google account; neither is constrained to users within your organization.

finding_sp_recommendation.format: Free text with a Console URL and the remediation steps.

examples.value: Go to https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/example-bucket, click on the Permissions tab, and remove "allUsers" and "allAuthenticatedUsers" from the bucket's members.

finding_sp_exception_instructions.format: Free text naming a security mark to set.

examples.value: Add the security mark "allow_public_bucket_acl" to the asset with a value of "true" to prevent this finding from being activated again.

finding_sp_reactivation_count.format: A non-negative integer (seen as a float, 0.0, in the fixture).

finding_sp_resource_path.format: Multivalue: four separate string elements in the read fixture, most specific first (project, then two folders, then the organization).

examples.note: one of four elements in the fixtures ResourcePath array

finding_sp_severity_level.format: Title case, e.g. High; not the same vocabulary as the Finding API's severity enum (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW).

notification_config_name.quote: Name of the notification config that generated current notification.

resource_name.quote: The full resource name of the resource.

resource_parent.format: A full resource name for the parent (a project or an organization).
resource_parent.quote: The full resource name of resource's parent.

resource_parent_display_name.format: A human-readable project or organization name.
resource_parent_display_name.quote: The human readable name of resource's parent.

resource_project.quote: The full resource name of project that the resource belongs to.

resource_project_display_name.format: A GCP project id string, despite the field's own name.
resource_project_display_name.quote: The project ID that the resource belongs to.
